small-claims.1A: Used to list the remaining parties to a case when a court form does not have enough space for all of them on the first page. It is attached right after that first page.
small-claims.1A.1: Lists the remaining debtors when a certificate of judgment, a writ of seizure and sale of personal property or of land, or a direction to enforce a writ of seizure and sale of personal property lacks space for all of them. It is attached to that form.
small-claims.1B: Used by a party to ask to change how the party, their representative or a witness attends a step. The request sets out the party's reasons and is served and filed, with proof of service, at least 30 days before the hearing date.
small-claims.1C: Used by a party to object to a request to change how someone attends a step. It is served and filed, with proof of service, no later than seven days after being served with the request.
small-claims.4A: Filled in by a person acting as litigation guardian for someone under a disability. It states the nature of the disability, the guardian's relationship to that person, and that the guardian has no interest in the case against that person's interest.
small-claims.4B: The affidavit (sworn statement) supporting a motion for an order about money payable to a person under disability under an order or settlement, such as an order paying it out of court. It is used instead of an affidavit in Form 15A.
small-claims.5A: Served with the claim by a plaintiff suing a partnership under its firm name, when the plaintiff wants an order that could be enforced personally against someone as a partner.
small-claims.7A: The form used to start a case. A plaintiff files it with the clerk, with a copy for each defendant, and it is served personally or by an alternative to personal service.
small-claims.8A: A sworn statement by the person who served a document, used to prove that the document was served.
small-claims.8B: Used by a lawyer or paralegal to prove service of a document that they served or caused to be served, when they are satisfied the service was done.
small-claims.9A: The form a defendant uses to dispute a plaintiff's claim. A defendant who disputes the claim serves it on every other party and files it, with proof of service, within 20 days of being served with the claim.
small-claims.9B: A request to the clerk, used for things such as asking to note a defendant in default, asking for an assessment hearing, or disputing a proposal by asking for a terms of payment hearing.
small-claims.10A: A defendant's claim against the plaintiff, or against another person where it arises out of the transaction or occurrence the plaintiff relies on or relates to the plaintiff's claim. It may be issued within 20 days after the defence is filed, or later, before trial or default judgment, with leave.
small-claims.11A: A sworn statement filed with the clerk to prove a case was properly brought in that court's area when all defendants were served outside it. The clerk needs this proof before noting any defendant in default.
small-claims.11B: The judgment the clerk may sign against a defendant who has been noted in default, for a debt or a set amount of money, including interest if claimed. The clerk serves it on all parties by mail or email.
small-claims.11.2A: Asks the clerk for an order on consent granting certain kinds of relief listed in the rules, such as setting aside a noting in default or dismissing an action. The request is signed by all parties. If refused, the clerk serves the request on all parties with reasons.
small-claims.11.3A: Used by a plaintiff to discontinue (drop) their claim against a defendant who did not file a defence in time. The plaintiff serves it on all defendants who were served with the claim and files it with proof of service.
small-claims.13A: A list of the witnesses a party plans to call and other people who know about the matters in dispute. Each party serves and files it at least 14 days before the date of the settlement conference.
small-claims.13B: A consent of the parties, used for example to allow matters discussed at a settlement or trial management conference to be disclosed, or, where the amount in dispute is under the appealable limit, signed by all parties so a judge may order final judgment at the settlement conference.
small-claims.14A: A form that may be used to make an offer to settle a case.
small-claims.14B: A form that may be used to accept an offer to settle.
small-claims.14C: A form that may be used to withdraw an offer to settle.
small-claims.14D: Used to set out the terms of an offer to settle that has been accepted.
small-claims.15A: The form used to bring a motion, combining the notice of motion and a supporting affidavit (sworn statement). A plaintiff may also use it to ask for a motion in writing for an assessment of damages.
small-claims.15B: A general affidavit (sworn statement) form that may be used when the rules allow or require an affidavit and no other form is named. A party responding to a motion serves and files it at least two days before the hearing date.
small-claims.18A: Used by a party to require a person in Ontario to come to a trial as a witness. It is served personally at least 10 days before the trial date, with attendance money paid or offered to the witness.
small-claims.18B: A warrant a trial judge may issue to all police officers in Ontario to apprehend a witness and bring the witness before the court, when a witness whose evidence is material fails to attend or remain at the trial as required by a summons to witness served on the witness.
small-claims.20A: Issued by the clerk, at the creditor's request, to the clerk at the court location the creditor names, when there is default under an order to pay money. The request is supported by an affidavit stating the amount still owing.
small-claims.20B: Used to enforce an order to deliver personal property. The clerk issues it to a bailiff at the request of the person the order favours, with an affidavit stating the property has not been delivered.
small-claims.20C: Used to enforce an order to pay money by having a bailiff seize and sell personal property. The clerk issues it at the creditor's request, supported by an affidavit stating the amount still owing.
small-claims.20D: Used to enforce an order to pay money through the seizure and sale of land. The clerk issues it to the sheriff at the creditor's request, supported by an affidavit stating the amount still owing.
small-claims.20E: Issued by the clerk to enforce an order to pay money through garnishment, naming a garnishee. The creditor serves it on the debtor and on the garnishee.
small-claims.20E.1: Used to renew a notice of garnishment before it expires. It is filed with the clerk of the court that issued the notice of garnishment, together with an affidavit for enforcement request.
small-claims.20F: A statement a garnishee files with the court setting out the particulars. The rules say certain garnishees file it within 10 days after service of the notice of garnishment.
small-claims.20G: Sent by a creditor to any co-owners of a debt, with a copy of the garnishee's statement, after the creditor is served with that statement.
small-claims.20H: Issued by the clerk at a creditor's request, when there is default under an order to pay money, directed to the debtor or another person to be examined. The creditor serves it personally or by an alternative to personal service.
small-claims.20I: A form an individual debtor completes for an examination, serving it on the creditor but not filing it with the court, and giving a copy to the judge. The clerk also serves it on an individual defendant with a notice of hearing.
small-claims.20J: A warrant the clerk issues when a court at a contempt hearing orders a person jailed, directed to all police officers in Ontario to apprehend the person named in it anywhere in Ontario and promptly bring the person to the nearest correctional institution.
small-claims.20K: A form that may be filed with the clerk to help the police apprehend a witness or a person named in a warrant of committal.
small-claims.20L: Served by a creditor or plaintiff on a debtor or defendant who fails to make payments as required under a payment proposal or an order for periodic payment.
small-claims.20M: A sworn statement filed when payments were not made as required under a payment proposal or an order for periodic payment. For a proposal, it states the amount paid and the unpaid balance.
small-claims.20N: Used to renew a writ of seizure and sale before it expires, by filing it with the bailiff (for personal property) or the sheriff (for land).
small-claims.20O: Filed by a creditor with the bailiff to ask for enforcement of a writ of seizure and sale of personal property.
small-claims.20P: A sworn statement stating the amount still owing, used to support a creditor's requests to the clerk to enforce an order to pay money. It is also served on the debtor with a notice of garnishment.
small-claims.20Q: Served by the person asking for a garnishment hearing, after getting a hearing date from the clerk, on the creditor, debtor, garnishee, any co-owner of the debt and other interested persons.
small-claims.20R: Served by a creditor on the garnishee and the clerk once the amount owing under an order enforced by garnishment is paid.

family.1.4: A request a party serves on every other party and files to ask the court for an order to stay (pause) or dismiss under rule 1.4.
family.1.4A: A notice the court clerk gives to the parties, when the court directs, saying that the case or motion may be stayed (paused) or dismissed.
family.4: Used by a party to choose a licensed representative, change representatives, or stop being represented and act in person. It is served on every other party and filed. In a child protection case scheduled for trial or on a trial list, acting in person needs the court's advance permission.
family.6: An acknowledgment of service in the form of a prepaid return postcard, mailed with a document. The person served signs it, and the signed postcard is filed in the continuing record.
family.6A: The form used when the court orders that a document be served by advertisement.
family.6B: An affidavit of service, which the rules list as one way to prove that a document was served.
family.6C: A certificate from a lawyer or paralegal, which the rules list as one way to prove that a document was served, where the lawyer or paralegal served it or caused it to be served.
family.8: One of the application forms a person files to start a family case. This is the general version.
family.8.0.1: An automatic order that the court clerk issues when certain claims are made, and gives to the party making the claim.
family.8A: An application form a person files to start a divorce case.
family.8B: An application form a person files to start a child protection case or a status review case.
family.8B.1: An application form filed to start a status review for a child in extended society care or a child formerly in extended society care.
family.8B.2: The general application form for cases under the Child, Youth and Family Services Act, 2017, other than child protection and status review cases.
family.8C: An application form a person files to start a case about secure treatment.
family.8D: An application form a person files to start an adoption case.
family.8D.1: An application form filed to ask the court to go ahead without (dispense with) a parent's consent to adoption before the child is placed.
family.8D.2: A notice, served under the Act, that a child is intended to be placed for adoption.
family.8D.3: A notice that a First Nations, Inuk or Métis child is intended to be placed for adoption. It is served on the child and on a representative chosen by each of the child's bands and First Nations, Inuit or Métis communities.
family.10: One of the answer forms a person against whom an application is made serves on every other party and files, within 30 days after being served with the application. The rules set different times in some cases, such as an application served outside Canada or the United States of America.
family.10A: A reply a party may serve and file to respond to a claim made in an answer. The rules say this may be done within 10 days after being served with an answer.
family.12: Used by a party who does not want to continue with all or part of a case to withdraw all or part of an application, answer or reply. It is also used to withdraw an appeal.
family.13: A financial statement used when a case includes a claim for support but not a property claim or a claim for exclusive possession of the matrimonial home and its contents.
family.13.1: A financial statement used when a case includes a property claim, with or without a support claim.
family.13A: A certificate a party serves together with financial disclosure documents to confirm they were served, and then files before a case conference.
family.13B: A net family property statement, which a party in a case with a property claim under Part I of the Family Law Act serves and files.
family.13C: Compares the parties' net family property statements. The parties file one together before a settlement conference, or if they cannot agree, each party serves and files their own.
family.14: The notice used to bring a motion. The rules say a motion requires a notice of motion and an affidavit, and may be supported by additional evidence.
family.14A: The general affidavit form. The rules say a motion requires a notice of motion and an affidavit, and the rules also use this form in other situations.
family.14B: A motion form that may be used instead of a notice of motion and affidavit when a motion is limited to procedural, uncomplicated or unopposed matters. The rules also require or allow it for certain other motions they name.
family.14C: A confirmation of motion that a party gives to the clerk, after giving a copy to every other party. If it is no longer correct, a corrected confirmation is given.
family.14D: An order made on a motion without notice. The rules say it requires the matter to come back to the court and, if possible, to the same judge, within 14 days or on a date chosen by the court.
family.15: Used by a party who wants to ask the court to change a final order or agreement. It is served and filed with all required attachments.
family.15B: Used by a party who does not agree to a requested change to a final order or agreement, or who wants the court to make an additional or different change.
family.15C: Filled in by a party who agrees to a requested change to a final order or agreement, or when the parties agree to a different change.
family.15D: Used when the parties, and any assignee, agree to change a final order or agreement only in relation to a child support obligation. The rules say parties who bring the motion this way do not need to serve or file financial statements.
family.17: A case conference notice, which a party who asks for a case conference serves and files.
family.17A: The general case conference brief used for a case conference.
family.17B: The case conference brief used for a case conference in a protection application or status review.
family.17C: The general settlement conference brief used for a settlement conference.
family.17D: The settlement conference brief used for a settlement conference in a protection application or status review.
family.17E: The brief used for a trial management conference held in the Ontario Court of Justice.
family.17F: A confirmation of conference that a party gives to the clerk, after giving a copy to every other party (except in a child protection case). If it is no longer correct, a corrected confirmation is given.
family.17G: A certificate of dispute resolution, which each party files in the situation the rules describe.
family.20: A request for information that a party serves on another party when getting information by affidavit or by another method.
family.20A: An authorization the clerk issues, where necessary, to a commissioner who is to supervise a questioning outside Ontario.
family.20B: A letter of request the clerk issues, where necessary, asking a court or authorities outside Ontario for help getting a person to come before the commissioner to be questioned.
family.20.2: An acknowledgement of the expert's duty, signed by the expert. The rules say it is included with an expert's report.
family.22: Used by a party to ask another party to admit, for purposes of the case only, that a fact is true or that a document is genuine.
family.22A: A response to a request to admit, used to deny or refuse to admit a fact or document. Unless a party serves a response within 20 days, the party is considered to have admitted it.
family.23: A summons a party serves on a witness, with the witness fee, so the witness gives evidence in court or is questioned and brings documents or other things.
family.23A: A summons to a witness outside Ontario under the Interprovincial Summonses Act.
family.23B: A court order to a prisoner's custodian to deliver the prisoner, when the prisoner needs to come to court or to be questioned.
family.23C: An affidavit that may be used as evidence at an uncontested trial, unless the court directs that oral evidence be given.
family.25: The general form for a court order. The rules say the party in whose favour an order is made prepares a draft of it, unless the court orders otherwise.
family.25A: The form for a divorce order. The rules say the party in whose favour an order is made prepares a draft of it, unless the court orders otherwise.
family.25B: The form for a secure treatment order. The rules say the party in whose favour an order is made prepares a draft of it, unless the court orders otherwise.
family.25C: The form for an adoption order. The rules say the party in whose favour an order is made prepares a draft of it, unless the court orders otherwise.
family.25D: The form for an order made after an uncontested trial. The rules say the party in whose favour an order is made prepares a draft of it, unless the court orders otherwise.
family.25E: Served by a party who disagrees with the form or content of a draft order, together with a copy of the order redrafted as proposed.
family.25F: The form used for a restraining order.
family.25G: The form used for a restraining order made on a motion without notice.
family.25H: The form used for an order that ends (terminates) a restraining order.
family.26: A statement of money owed under an order that is in default, with a copy of that order attached.
family.26A: An affidavit filed with the sheriff or clerk that sets out items of expense.
family.26B: An affidavit used to file a domestic contract with the court under the Family Law Act.
family.26C: A notice sent immediately by a person who continues an enforcement after it is transferred between a recipient and the Director under subrule (12) or (13), to all parties to the enforcement, to the clerk at every court office involved, and to every sheriff involved.
family.26D: An affidavit used to file a family arbitration award for support with the court under the Family Law Act.
family.27: A request a recipient may serve on the payor for a financial statement when a payment order is in default.
family.27A: A request a recipient may serve on an income source of the payor, when a payment order is in default, requiring the income source to send the recipient a statement of income.
family.27B: A statement of income that a payor's income source prepares and sends to the recipient after receiving a request, when a payment order is in default.
family.27C: An appointment a recipient may serve on the payor when a payment order is in default, requiring the payor to come to a financial examination and bring documents or things named in it.
family.28: A writ of seizure and sale that the clerk issues when a recipient files a request for it and a statement of money owed.
family.28A: Filed by a recipient, along with a statement of money owed, to ask the clerk to issue a writ of seizure and sale.
family.28B: A statutory declaration to the sheriff. The rules say it may be filed with the sheriff when a court changes a payment order that is being enforced by a writ of seizure and sale.
family.28C: A writ the court may, on a motion with special service, give permission to issue, directing the sheriff to take and hold all or part of the land and other property of a person against whom an order has been made, and any income from it.
family.29: Filed by a recipient, along with a statement of money owed, to ask the clerk to issue notices of garnishment.
family.29A: A notice of garnishment for a lump-sum debt. The clerk issues it when a recipient files a request for garnishment and a statement of money owed.
family.29B: A notice of garnishment for a periodic debt. The clerk issues it when a recipient files a request for garnishment and a statement of money owed.
family.29C: A notice the garnishee sends to another person who co-owns a debt being garnished, by mail, fax or email to that person's address in the garnishee's records.
family.29D: A statutory declaration a recipient may serve on the garnishee and the payor, and file with the court, setting out the new amount to be paid when a support order indexes payments for inflation.
family.29E: The form a payor uses to dispute a notice of garnishment or a statutory declaration of indexed support, served on the other parties and filed with the court.
family.29F: The form a garnishee uses to dispute a notice of garnishment or a statutory declaration of indexed support, served on the other parties and filed with the court.
family.29G: The form a co-owner of a debt uses to dispute a notice of garnishment or a statutory declaration of indexed support, served on the other parties and filed with the court.
family.29H: A notice of a hearing about a garnishment. The clerk issues it on request after a dispute is served and filed, or if the recipient says the garnishee has not paid any money or enough money.
family.29I: Sent by a recipient to the garnishee and payor, and filed with the clerk, to stop a garnishment when the recipient no longer wants to enforce by garnishment, or periodic payments have ended and all other amounts owing have been paid.
family.29J: A statement about support, given to a financial institution that is a garnishee.
family.30: A notice of a default hearing about a support order being enforced. The clerk issues it after the recipient files a request and a statement of money owed, or after the Director files a statement of money owed.
family.30A: Filed by a recipient who is enforcing a support order, along with a statement of money owed, to ask the clerk to issue a notice of default hearing.
family.30B: The form a payor serves on the recipient and files, together with a financial statement, after being served with a notice of default hearing.
family.31: The notice used to bring a contempt motion. The rules say it is served with a supporting affidavit by special service, unless the court orders otherwise.
family.32: A bond the court may order a person to post. It lists the court's conditions and an amount of money to be forfeited if they are not obeyed, and has at least one surety unless the court orders otherwise.
family.32A: Served by a person asking the court's permission to enforce a bond, with a copy of the bond attached, on the person said to have broken the bond and on each surety.
family.32B: A warrant for arrest. One use in the rules is to bring before the court a witness who was served with a summons as the rules require and did not obey it, when it is necessary to have the witness present in court or at a questioning.
family.32C: An affidavit a party uses to support a motion for a warrant of committal, for example stating that a person in contempt has not obeyed a condition the court imposed.
family.32D: The warrant of committal issued to enforce an order of imprisonment.
family.32.1: Filed by a person entitled to enforcement of a family arbitration award to ask the court to enforce it, together with the family arbitration agreement, the certificates of independent legal advice, and the award.
family.32.1A: The form a respondent serves on every other party and files to oppose a request to enforce a family arbitration award.
family.33: The form for an information for a warrant to bring a child to a place of safety, used in a child protection case.
family.33A: The warrant, in a child protection case, to bring a child to a place of safety.
family.33B: The plan of care for a child used by a children's aid society in a child protection case, whether the society is the applicant or a respondent giving its answer.
family.33B.1: Used in a child protection case by a party other than a children's aid society to set out its plan of care for a child and, if it is a respondent, its answer.
family.33B.2: The answer a respondent uses in cases under the Child, Youth and Family Services Act, 2017 other than child protection and status review, such as an application for an openness order or to change or end one.
family.33C: A statement of the facts the parties agree on in a child protection case.
family.33D: A statement of the facts the parties agree on in a status review application.
family.33D.1: The application used to start a case to publish something or make it public under O. Reg. 155/18 of the Child, Youth and Family Services Act, 2017.
family.33D.2: A consent to publishing something or making it public under O. Reg. 155/18 of the Child, Youth and Family Services Act, 2017.
family.33D.3: The answer a respondent serves and files in response to an application to publish or make public under O. Reg. 155/18 of the Child, Youth and Family Services Act, 2017.
family.33E: The consent signed by the child in an application for secure treatment under the Child, Youth and Family Services Act, 2017.
family.33F: The consent signed by a person other than the child in an application for secure treatment under the Child, Youth and Family Services Act, 2017.
family.34: The child's consent to being adopted. A representative of the Children's Lawyer witnesses it and completes the affidavit of execution and independent legal advice in the form.
family.34A: An affidavit of parentage, filed with an adoption application when the child is not in extended society care. The rules accept it or any other evidence about parentage that the court requires from the child's parent or a person named by the court.
family.34B: A consent to a child's adoption, used in an adoption case when the applicant has a spouse who has not joined in the application.
family.34C: A statement on an adoption from a Director or local director, filed in an adoption case when the Act or an order requires it.
family.34D: An affidavit signed by an adoption applicant giving details about their education, work, health, background, ability to care for the child, relationship with the child, and whether the child is a First Nations, Inuk or Métis person.
family.34E: A Director's consent to adoption, filed with an adoption application when the child is in extended society care.
family.34F: A consent to adoption under section 180 of the Act from each parent, other than the applicant, known to the person placing the child or an applicant. Filed when the child is not in extended society care and is placed by a licensee or children's aid society.
family.34G: An affidavit signed by the adoption licensee or an authorized children's aid society employee, depending on who is placing the child. It is filed with an adoption application when the child is not in extended society care and is placed by a licensee or society.
family.34G.1: An affidavit signed by a children's aid society employee in the adoption of a child who is in extended society care.
family.34H: An affidavit from each applicant in a family adoption, filed when the child was a resident of Canada before being placed for adoption. For an applicant who is not a parent of the child, it contains a broad record check or proof that one was requested.
family.34H.1: In a family adoption of a child resident in Canada before placement, an affidavit from each person over 18, other than an applicant or child, who lives with a non-parent applicant and is not a parent of the child. It contains a broad record check or proof of request.
family.34I: The consent of a child's parent when the parent's spouse applies to adopt the child.
family.34J: Completed by a representative of the Children's Lawyer who witnesses the adoption consent of a parent who is under the age of 18 years.
family.34K: A certificate the clerk prepares in an adoption case after reviewing the application and other documents to see whether they are in order, before it goes to a judge.
family.34L: The application used to start a case asking the court for an openness order.
family.34M: A consent to an openness order under section 194 of the Child, Youth and Family Services Act, 2017.
family.34M.1: A consent to an openness order under section 196 or 197 of the Child, Youth and Family Services Act, 2017.
family.34N: The application used to start a case asking the court to change or end an openness order.
family.35.1: An affidavit a party claiming decision-making responsibility, parenting time or contact with a child serves and files with the claim. A non-parent claiming decision-making responsibility attaches a police records check or other proof set out in the rules.
family.35.1A: An affidavit filed with a claim about a child when the child or any party has been involved in a child protection case or received services from a child protection agency. It is not filed in the continuing record.
family.36: An affidavit filed in a divorce case that contains the information the rules list.
family.36A: A certificate the clerk prepares in a divorce case before presenting the documents to a judge.
family.36B: The divorce certificate issued once the matters set out in the rules are satisfied. Unless the court orders otherwise, it is mailed to the parties if stamped envelopes were filed, or emailed.
family.37: A notice of hearing the clerk serves on a respondent when documents come from a designated authority or another court, along with copies of those documents and blank response forms.
family.37A: An information sheet the clerk sends, with a copy of the notice of hearing, to the designated authority, or to the applicant and the originating court.
family.37B: A court's direction asking for further information or documents, with the court's reasons for requesting further evidence attached.
family.37C: A notice the clerk prepares when the court receives further information or documents, and sends with copies of them to the respondent so the hearing can continue.
family.37D: A notice the Ontario court clerk gives to a party believed to ordinarily reside in Ontario, saying that an order made outside Canada has been registered.
family.37E: A notice the clerk sends to an applicant, with copies of the documents from the confirming court, when that court asks for further evidence about a provisional order.
family.38: The notice of appeal that starts an appeal from an Ontario Court of Justice order to the Superior Court of Justice under listed provisions. It is served on every other party affected by the appeal or entitled to appeal, and on the clerk where the order was made.
family.39: A notice the clerk serves on the parties by mail or email when a case has not been settled, withdrawn, or scheduled or adjourned for trial within the time set in the rules.
family.43: The request and consent each party serves and files, with a motion form, to ask for a binding judicial dispute resolution hearing.
family.43A: The version of the binding judicial dispute resolution hearing request and consent used by the Office of the Children's Lawyer, served and filed with a motion form.
family.43B: An affidavit that may be used for a binding judicial dispute resolution hearing.
family.43C: A confirmation of a binding judicial dispute resolution hearing that each party gives to every other party, by mail, fax, email or another method, before giving it to the clerk.

civil.1A: The notice a party delivers to object to the proposed method of attendance at a hearing or step.
civil.2.1A: A request a party serves on every other party and files with proof of service, asking for an order for a stay or dismissal under rule 2.1.
civil.2.1B: The notice the registrar gives the parties, when the court directs, saying that the proceeding may be stayed or dismissed.
civil.2.2A: The notice of motion used to ask for a vexatious litigant order. It sets out the grounds for the order and is served on the person the order is sought against and on every party to a proceeding listed in the notice.
civil.2.2B: The notice of application used to ask for a vexatious litigant order. It sets out the grounds for the order and is served on the person the order is sought against and on every party to a proceeding listed in the notice.
civil.2.2C: The notice a registrar prepares, when a judge gives written direction, proposing consideration of a vexatious litigant order against a party to an ongoing proceeding.
civil.2.2D: The response the person who may become the subject of a vexatious litigant order may serve and file within 20 days after receiving a notice about it.
civil.2.2E: A reply that a moving party, applicant or notified person may serve and file about a possible vexatious litigant order, after a response is received or if no response is served.
civil.2.2F: The order a judge makes after an initial review of the notice and submissions, either directing that a hearing be held or dismissing the matter, with reasons.
civil.2.2G: The vexatious litigant order a judge makes, with reasons, following a hearing.
civil.4A: The standard heading placed on documents in an action. It sets out the name of the court, the court file number and the title of the proceeding.
civil.4B: The form used for the general heading of documents in an application.
civil.4C: The backsheet placed on every document in a proceeding. It sets out details such as the short title of the proceeding, the court, the court file number and the title of the document.
civil.4D: The form for an affidavit used in a proceeding. It is written in the first person, states the full name of the person making it, and is divided into numbered paragraphs.
civil.4E: A requisition a party files, paying any prescribed fee, when entitled to require the registrar to carry out a duty under the rules; a person entitled to see a document in the court file may also file one to obtain a certified copy.
civil.4F: The form used for a notice of constitutional question under the Courts of Justice Act.
civil.7A: A notice the registrar sends to someone who started, continued or filed a document for a party under disability without filing the required affidavit. It requires the affidavit to be filed no later than 15 days after receipt of the notice.
civil.7B: A request another party serves on every other party and files with proof of service before that party may move to appoint a litigation guardian for a party known or believed to be under disability.
civil.7C: An order from the registrar allowing a minor who has reached the age of majority to continue the proceeding without the litigation guardian. It is obtained by filing an affidavit saying the minor has reached that age.
civil.8A: A notice a plaintiff or applicant suing a partnership in the firm name may serve with the originating process on a person, stating that the person was a partner at a material time, when seeking an order enforceable personally against that person as a partner.
civil.11A: An order from the registrar allowing a proceeding to continue when a party's interest or liability is transferred or transmitted while the proceeding is pending. It is obtained by filing an affidavit verifying the transfer or transmission.
civil.14A: The general statement of claim, the document that starts an action.
civil.14B: The statement of claim used to start a mortgage action for foreclosure.
civil.14C: Used to start an action when there is not enough time to prepare a statement of claim. It contains a short statement of the nature of the claim.
civil.14D: The statement of claim a plaintiff files in an action that was started by a notice of action. The rule says it is filed within thirty days after the notice of action is issued.
civil.14E: The notice of application, a document that starts an application. It states the exact relief sought, the grounds to be argued and the documentary evidence to be used at the hearing.
civil.14E.1: The notice of application used for an application under subsection 140 (3) of the Courts of Justice Act. It states the exact relief sought, the grounds to be argued and the documentary evidence to be used at the hearing.
civil.14F: Information for court use, filed together with a statement of claim, notice of action or notice of application, unless that document is filed electronically through an online portal.
civil.15A: Used by a party who has a lawyer of record to change to a new lawyer. It gives the new lawyer's name, address and telephone number and is served and filed with proof of service.
civil.15B: Used by a party acting in person to appoint a lawyer of record. It gives the lawyer's name, address and telephone number and is served on every other party and filed with proof of service.
civil.15C: Used by a party with a lawyer of record to elect to act in person, giving an address for service and telephone number; served and filed with proof of service. Not available to a party under disability or acting in a representative capacity, or to a corporation without leave.
civil.16A: A card mailed with a document being served. Service this way is only effective as of the date the sender receives the card.
civil.16B: An affidavit by the person who served a document, used to prove that the document was served.
civil.16B.1: A certificate a lawyer may use to prove service of a document that the lawyer served or had served.
civil.16C: A certificate used to prove that a sheriff served a document, either personally or at a place of residence.
civil.17A: A request for service of court or other legal documents abroad. It is one of the forms that can be used to prove service made in a country that is part of the Convention.
civil.17B: A summary of the document to be served, one of the Convention forms (17A to 17C) that the rules allow for proving service made in a contracting state under the Convention.
civil.17C: A notice and summary of a document being served. It is one of the forms that can be used to prove service made in a country that is part of the Convention.
civil.18A: The statement of defence, the document a defendant delivers after being served with a statement of claim. It may also include a counterclaim or a crossclaim.
civil.18B: Used by a defendant who has been served with a statement of claim and intends to defend the action. It is delivered within the time prescribed for delivery of a statement of defence.
civil.19A: The form of default judgment used for a claim for a debt or liquidated demand in money, including interest if claimed in the statement of claim.
civil.19B: The form of default judgment used for a claim to recover possession of land.
civil.19C: The form of default judgment used for a claim to recover possession of personal property.
civil.19D: The requisition a plaintiff files with the registrar before default judgment is signed. It states that the claim is one for which default judgment may be signed and whether any partial payment has been made.
civil.22A: A special case sets out the facts the parties agree on so the court can decide the question stated. It includes any documents needed and the relief the parties agree on.
civil.23A: Used by a plaintiff to discontinue all or part of an action against a defendant before the close of pleadings. It is served on all parties who were served with the statement of claim and filed with proof of service.
civil.23B: Used by a defendant who has counterclaimed to choose to go ahead with the counterclaim after the action is discontinued or dismissed for delay. The rules say it is delivered within thirty days after the discontinuance or the dismissal.
civil.23C: Used by a defendant to withdraw all or part of a statement of defence with respect to a plaintiff, delivered to all parties. Leave of the court is needed if the defendant has crossclaimed or made a third party claim, and withdrawing an admission is governed by rule 51.05.
civil.24.1A: A notice filed with the mediation co-ordinator stating the mediator's name and the date of the mediation session.
civil.24.1B: A notice the assigned mediator serves on every party giving the place, date, time and method of attendance for the mediation session, and advising that attendance is obligatory.
civil.24.1C: A statement of issues each party prepares and gives to every other party and to the mediator. The rule says this is done at least seven days before the mediation session.
civil.24.1D: A certificate a mediator files with the mediation co-ordinator after cancelling a mediation session because a party did not provide the required statement of issues or did not attend within the first 30 minutes.
civil.25A: The reply, one of the pleadings in an action along with the statement of claim and the statement of defence, if there is one.
civil.27A: A counterclaim against parties to the main action only. It is included in the same document as the statement of defence, which is titled a statement of defence and counterclaim.
civil.27B: A counterclaim against the plaintiff and a person not already a party to the main action. It is included in the same document as the statement of defence, which is titled a statement of defence and counterclaim.
civil.27C: The defence to a counterclaim, delivered by the plaintiff and any other defendant to the counterclaim who is already a party to the main action. The rule says it is delivered within twenty days after service of the statement of defence and counterclaim.
civil.27D: A reply to a defence to counterclaim, if there is one. The rule says it is delivered within ten days after service of the defence to counterclaim.
civil.28A: A crossclaim, included in the same document as the statement of defence, which is titled a statement of defence and crossclaim.
civil.28B: The defence to a crossclaim, one of the pleadings in a crossclaim.
civil.28C: A reply to a defence to crossclaim, if there is one. The rule says it is delivered within ten days after service of the defence to crossclaim.
civil.29A: The form used for a third party claim, including a fourth or later party claim or a claim by a defendant to a counterclaim or crossclaim.
civil.29B: The defence a third party delivers to defend against a third party claim. It is also used for a defence by a fourth or later party.
civil.29C: A reply to a third party defence, if there is one. The rule says it is delivered within ten days after service of the third party defence.
civil.30A: An affidavit of documents made by an individual party and served on every other party. It discloses all documents relevant to any matter in issue in the action that are or have been in the party's possession, control or power.
civil.30B: An affidavit of documents made by a corporation or partnership and served on every other party. It discloses all documents relevant to any matter in issue in the action that are or have been in the party's possession, control or power.
civil.30C: A request one party serves on another to inspect documents that are not privileged and are listed in the other party's affidavit of documents.
civil.34A: A notice of examination served when the person to be examined is a party to the proceeding. It is served on the party's lawyer of record, or on the party if acting in person.
civil.34B: A summons to witness for an examination out of court, served personally on a person who lives in Ontario and is neither a party nor a person referred to in subrule (2) or (3).
civil.34C: A commission authorizing a named commissioner to take evidence from a person who is to be examined outside Ontario.
civil.34D: A letter of request to the judicial authorities where a person outside Ontario is found, asking them to issue what is needed to make that person attend and be examined.
civil.34E: The court order used when a person is to be examined outside Ontario. If the moving party asks, it provides for issuing a commission and a letter of request.
civil.35A: A list of written questions for an examination for discovery, served on the person to be examined and every other party.
civil.35B: An affidavit giving the answers of the person being examined to written questions on an examination for discovery. The rule says it is served on the examining party within fifteen days after service of the list of questions.
civil.37A: The notice of motion, the document used to make a motion unless the nature of the motion or the circumstances make it unnecessary or the rules say otherwise.
civil.37B: A confirmation of motion that a party making a motion on notice gives the registrar before the hearing, by email or at the court office, with a copy emailed to the other party. A responding party may give one if the moving party fails to send a copy.
civil.37C: A chart the moving party serves and files on a motion to compel answers or have undertakings satisfied, setting out each issue, the question number with its transcript page, and the exact words of the question. The responding party completes and returns it.
civil.38A: A notice of appearance, which a respondent who has been served with a notice of application delivers right away (forthwith).
civil.38B: A confirmation of application that a party making an application on notice gives the registrar before the hearing, by email or at the court office, with a copy emailed to the other party. A corrected one is given if it is no longer correct.
civil.42A: A certificate of pending litigation under the Courts of Justice Act, which a registrar may issue only under an order of the court.
civil.43A: An interpleader order about property that two or more other persons claim. It is sought by a person who claims no beneficial interest in the property and is willing to deposit it with the court or deal with it as the court directs.
civil.44A: A bond given as security in a proceeding for interim recovery of personal property. It stays in force until the security is released.
civil.47A: Used by a party to an action to have the issues of fact tried, or damages assessed, or both, by a jury. The rule says it is delivered at any time before the close of pleadings, unless a statute requires trial without a jury.
civil.48D: The order the registrar makes, unless the court orders otherwise and subject to exceptions, dismissing an action for delay that was not set down for trial or terminated by the fifth anniversary of its start, or was struck off a trial list and not restored by the second anniversary.
civil.49A: An offer to settle one or more of the claims in a proceeding, which a party may serve on any other party on the terms set out in the offer.
civil.49B: A notice that may be used to withdraw an offer to settle.
civil.49C: Used to accept an offer to settle by serving it on the party who made the offer, before the offer is withdrawn or the court disposes of the claim.
civil.49D: An offer one defendant may serve on another to contribute toward settling a claim, where two or more defendants are alleged to be jointly, or jointly and severally, liable to the plaintiff.
civil.49E: Used by the plaintiff to record the terms of a partial settlement agreement, other than any money amount. A copy is served on every other party and filed.
civil.50A: A certificate of readiness each party delivers before a pre-trial conference. It shows whether the party intends to call expert evidence at trial and gives details about each expert's report.
civil.51A: A request asking another party to admit, for the purposes of the proceeding only, that a fact is true or a document is authentic.
civil.51B: The response a party gives to a request to admit, served on the party who made the request. The rule says it is served within twenty days after the request is served.
civil.53: An acknowledgment of expert's duty, signed by the expert.
civil.53A: A summons a party may serve on a person in Ontario to attend a trial as a witness at the time and place stated. It may also require the witness to bring related documents or other things.
civil.53B: A warrant for arrest a presiding judge may issue when a witness whose evidence is material, who was served with a summons and paid or tendered proper attendance money, fails to attend or remain at the trial as the summons requires, so the witness is apprehended anywhere in Ontario.
civil.53C: A summons used to compel a witness outside Ontario to attend, under the Interprovincial Summonses Act.
civil.53D: An order the court may make directing the officer who has custody of a prisoner to bring them for an examination or to a hearing as a witness, where their evidence is material to an action.
civil.55A: A notice of a hearing for directions on a reference, served on every other party to the proceeding together with a copy of the order directing the reference.
civil.55B: A notice served on a person the referee adds as a party during a reference, together with the order adding them and the order directing the reference. Once served, the person becomes a party.
civil.55C: The form for a report on a reference in a proceeding to administer the estate of a person who has died.
civil.55D: A notice served on a claimant when their claim is contested on a reference, fixing a date for the claim to be decided.
civil.55E: A notice served on each creditor when money is to be paid out of court to creditors, saying that payment of the creditor's claim, as allowed, may be obtained from the Accountant.
civil.55F: The standard conditions of sale for a sale by auction or tender on a reference, subject to any changes the referee directs.
civil.55G: An interim report a referee may make on the result of a sale.
civil.56A: An order for security for costs. Until the security is given, the plaintiff or applicant it is made against may not take any step in the proceeding except an appeal from the order, unless the court orders otherwise.
civil.57A: A bill of costs that a party who is awarded costs serves on the other parties and files with proof of service. This happens after a trial, a motion that ends a proceeding, or the hearing of an application.
civil.57B: A costs outline, no more than three pages long, that a party intending to seek costs for a step in a proceeding gives to every other party involved in that step and brings to the hearing, unless the parties have agreed on the costs for that step.
civil.58A: A notice of appointment for assessment of costs, obtained from the assessment officer by a party entitled to costs after filing a bill of costs and the document giving the right to costs.
civil.58B: A notice a party liable to pay costs may obtain from the assessment officer when the party entitled to costs does not file or serve a bill of costs for assessment within a reasonable time.
civil.58C: A certificate in which the assessment officer sets out the amount of costs assessed and allowed.
civil.59A: The form for an order, including a draft order. It contains the name of the person who made the order, the date it was made, and the details needed to understand it.
civil.59B: The form used for a judgment. The rules mention a draft in this form being filed with a requisition after a judge declines to make a vexatious litigant order.
civil.59C: The form used for an order on appeal.
civil.59D: A notice of an appointment to have an order settled, served on the other parties who took part in the hearing or conference and filed with proof of service. The rules say this is at least seven days before the appointment.
civil.60A: A writ of seizure and sale, one way to enforce an order for paying or recovering money. A creditor obtains it by filing a requisition with the registrar where the proceeding was started.
civil.60B: A writ of sequestration directing a sheriff to take and hold the property of a person against whom an order was made, and collect its income, until the person complies. It may be issued only with leave of the court, obtained on motion.
civil.60C: A writ of possession, used to enforce an order for the recovery or delivery of possession of land. It may be issued only with leave of the court.
civil.60D: A writ of delivery, used to enforce an order for the recovery of possession of personal property other than money. It is obtained by filing a requisition with the registrar along with a copy of the order.
civil.60E: A request filed with the sheriff to renew a writ of seizure and sale before it expires. The sheriff records the renewal date and the new expiration date.
civil.60F: A direction filed with the sheriff, along with a copy of the order, to enforce a writ of seizure and sale. It sets out details such as the date of the order, the amount awarded and the interest rate.
civil.60G: A requisition a creditor files with the registrar to enforce an order for payment or recovery of money by garnishment, together with a copy of the order and an affidavit.
civil.60G.1: Filed with the registrar, together with an affidavit, to renew a notice of garnishment before it expires.
civil.60H: The notice of garnishment the registrar issues once the creditor's requisition and affidavit are filed. It names as garnishees the people listed in the affidavit.
civil.60H.1: The notice of renewal of garnishment the registrar issues once a requisition for renewal and affidavit are filed. It names as garnishees the people listed in the affidavit.
civil.60I: A garnishee's statement. A blank copy is attached to the notice of garnishment served on the garnishee; a garnishee who disputes the garnishment or pays the sheriff less than the notice's amount serves it on the creditor and debtor and files it.
civil.60I.1: Served by a creditor on co-owners of a debt, with a copy of the garnishee's statement, when that statement shows the debt is owed to the debtor and to one or more co-owners.
civil.60J: Served by the creditor on the garnishee and the sheriff when the amount owing under an order enforced by garnishment has been paid.
civil.60K: A warrant a judge may issue to arrest a person against whom a contempt order is sought, when the judge thinks the person's attendance at the hearing is necessary and the person is not likely to attend voluntarily.
civil.60L: A warrant of committal, which the rules say may be used to enforce an order for imprisonment that a judge makes after a finding of contempt on a motion for a contempt order.
civil.60M: The notice a sheriff sends to creditors who have filed enforcement process with the sheriff, telling them a claim has been received. Each creditor then tells the sheriff in writing whether they admit or dispute the claim.
civil.60N: The report a sheriff mails or emails to a party or lawyer who filed a writ and asked in writing how the sheriff carried out that writ.
civil.60O: A written request a debtor gives the sheriff to withdraw a writ when the judgment debt has been released by an order of discharge or certificate of full performance under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act.
civil.61A: Used to ask the Divisional Court for permission (leave) to appeal. The notice states that the motion will be heard on a date fixed by the Registrar.
civil.61A.1: Used to ask the Court of Appeal for permission (leave) to appeal. The notice states that the motion will be heard on a date fixed by the Registrar.
civil.61A.2: Used to start an appeal to the Court of Appeal. It states the relief sought, the grounds of appeal, and the basis for the court's power to hear the appeal.
civil.61A.3: Used to start an appeal to the Divisional Court. It states the relief sought, the grounds of appeal, and the basis for the court's power to hear the appeal.
civil.61B: Shows the heading used on any document filed in an appeal.
civil.61C: Served and filed by the appellant with the notice of appeal, listing only the parts of the evidence that the appellant thinks are needed for the appeal.
civil.61D: Served and filed by the respondent in an appeal to confirm the appellant's certificate respecting evidence, or to add or remove parts of the evidence it lists.
civil.61E: Used to bring a cross-appeal. It states the relief sought and the grounds, and is served on all parties whose interests may be affected by the cross-appeal.
civil.61F: Used to change a notice of appeal or cross-appeal without the court's permission, before the appeal is perfected. It is served on the parties who got the original notice and filed with proof of service.
civil.61G: The notice the Registrar sends to everyone listed in the certificate of perfection once an appeal is perfected and placed on the list of cases to be heard.
civil.61H: A certificate in the appeal book and compendium stating that its contents are complete. The rules describe it as signed by the appellant's lawyer or someone the lawyer has authorized.
civil.61I: The order the Registrar makes dismissing an appeal or cross-appeal for delay, with fixed costs, in the situations the rules describe.
civil.61I.1: The order the Registrar makes, unless the court orders otherwise, dismissing an appeal to the Divisional Court for delay when the appeal has not been set down for hearing or otherwise ended within the time the rule sets, unless the appellant is under a disability.
civil.61J: The order the Registrar makes dismissing a motion for leave to appeal for delay, with fixed costs.
civil.61J.1: The order the Registrar makes dismissing a motion in an appeal court for delay, with fixed costs, when the moving party does not serve and file the needed documents in time, as the rules describe.
civil.61K: Delivered by a party to abandon (drop) an appeal or cross-appeal.
civil.61L: Delivered by a respondent who cross-appealed, when the appeal is dismissed for delay or abandoned, to say they elect to go ahead with the cross-appeal.
civil.61M: The notice of a motion, other than a motion for leave to appeal, that will be heard by a single judge of the Court of Appeal.
civil.61N: The notice of a motion, other than a motion for leave to appeal, that will be heard by a single judge of the Divisional Court.
civil.61O: The notice of a motion, other than a motion for leave to appeal, that will be heard by a panel of judges of the Court of Appeal.
civil.61P: The notice of a motion, other than a motion for leave to appeal, that will be heard by a panel of judges of the Divisional Court.
civil.62A: Used to start an appeal to a judge. It is served on all parties whose interests may be affected and states the relief sought and the grounds of appeal.
civil.63A: Issued by the registrar, when a party to the appeal asks, when an order is stayed. Once it is filed with the sheriff, the sheriff does not start or continue enforcing the order until satisfied the stay has ended.
civil.63B: A certificate of stay for an order of the Landlord and Tenant Board stayed under the Statutory Powers Procedure Act, issued by the appeal court's registrar when a party to the appeal asks. Once it is filed, the sheriff does not enforce the order until the stay ends.
civil.64A: Served and filed by a defendant in a foreclosure or sale action who wishes to redeem the mortgaged property.
civil.64B: The default judgment for foreclosure with a reference that the registrar signs when the plaintiff wants a reference about subsequent encumbrancers.
civil.64C: The default judgment for immediate foreclosure that the registrar signs at the plaintiff's request when a defendant in a foreclosure action is noted in default and has not filed a request to redeem, and the plaintiff does not want a reference about subsequent encumbrancers.
civil.64D: A default judgment for foreclosure of a mortgage without a reference.
civil.64E: A final order of foreclosure the plaintiff may get on motion without notice against a subsequent encumbrancer who was served with a notice of reference but did not attend and prove a claim, once the referee has reported this and the report is confirmed.
civil.64F: Served on the plaintiff and filed, with proof of service, by a defendant in a foreclosure action who wishes a sale instead, within the time the rules set. A subsequent encumbrancer must also pay security into court and give verified particulars of the claim.
civil.64G: A default judgment for sale with a redemption period, in an action converted from foreclosure to sale. The registrar signs it at the plaintiff's request after a request for sale.
civil.64H: A default judgment for immediate sale, in an action converted from foreclosure to sale. The registrar signs it at the plaintiff's request after a request for sale.
civil.64I: A default judgment for sale in an action converted from foreclosure to sale, conditional on a subsequent encumbrancer proving their claim. The registrar signs it at the plaintiff's request.
civil.64J: The default judgment for immediate sale with a reference that the registrar signs when a defendant in a sale action is noted in default and has not filed a request to redeem.
civil.64K: A default judgment for sale with a redemption period. The registrar signs it when a defendant in a sale action is noted in default and has filed a request to redeem.
civil.64L: A final order for sale that may be obtained on motion without notice when no defendant filed a request to redeem and no subsequent encumbrancer attended and proved a claim on the reference, once the referee has reported this and the report is confirmed.
civil.64M: The default judgment for redemption that the registrar signs in a redemption action when the defendant has been noted in default.
civil.64N: The notice of reference served on a subsequent encumbrancer who is added as a defendant on the reference.
civil.64O: The notice of reference the referee directs be served on a defendant named in the statement of claim who was not alleged there to be a subsequent encumbrancer but appears to have a lien, charge or encumbrance on the mortgaged property.
civil.64P: Served on those named as defendants in the statement of claim, listing all appearing to have a lien, charge or encumbrance on the mortgaged property and their claims. A named subsequent encumbrancer who filed no request to redeem or for sale is not entitled to notice of a foreclosure reference.
civil.64Q: A notice served on a defendant added on the reference who has an interest in the equity, together with the order and the judgment in the action.
civil.65A: A judgment for administration of an estate. The rules say it is granted only if the judge is satisfied the questions between the parties cannot otherwise be properly decided.
civil.66A: The form of a judgment for partition or sale.
civil.68A: Used to start an application to the Divisional Court for judicial review. It states the exact relief sought, the grounds to be argued, and the documentary evidence to be used at the hearing.
civil.68B: The notice the registrar sends to the parties and others named in the certificate of perfection once a judicial review application is placed on the list for hearing.
civil.68C: The order the registrar makes dismissing a judicial review application for delay, with costs fixed at $750, when the applicant does not fix the default within the time allowed after notice.
civil.68D: The order the Registrar makes, unless the court orders otherwise, dismissing an application for judicial review for delay when the application has not been set down for hearing or otherwise ended within the time the rule sets, unless the applicant is under a disability.
civil.72A: Served on every interested party by a person who pays money into court under an offer to settle or an acceptance of an offer. It is not filed with the court.
civil.72B: The affidavit that supports a motion to a judge for payment out of court of money held to the credit of a person under disability, except a motion made by the Children's Lawyer or the Public Guardian and Trustee.
civil.72C: An order the court may make, on a motion or application without notice by a person who claims to be entitled to money or securities held by the Accountant for another person's benefit, directing that they not be dealt with except on notice to that person.
civil.73A: Used to start an application to register a United Kingdom judgment. It states the exact relief sought, the grounds to be argued, and the documentary evidence to be used at the hearing.
civil.74A: Used to apply for a certificate of appointment of estate trustee. It is filed with other documents the rules list, such as proof of service and proof of death.
civil.74B: An affidavit used as proof of service of an application for a certificate of appointment of estate trustee.
civil.74B.1: The form used for a lawyer's certificate of service of an application for a certificate of appointment of estate trustee.
civil.74C: The certificate of appointment of estate trustee. A draft is filed with the application, with a copy of any will and codicils attached.
civil.74D: An affidavit about the signing (execution) of a will or codicil, which may be deposited with it. In applications for a certificate of appointment of estate trustee or a small estate certificate, a non-holograph will or codicil is attached as an exhibit to it or other evidence the rule describes.
civil.74E: An affidavit about the condition of a will or codicil at the time it was signed. It is used where the will or codicil has an alteration, erasure or other change that was not attested.
civil.74F: An affidavit stating that the handwriting and signature in a holograph will or codicil are those of the person who died.
civil.74G: Used by a person to renounce a right to act as estate trustee, or to consent to an application, in the estate situations the rules describe.
civil.74H: The form used to give consent.
civil.74I: A form for an order in an estates proceeding. The rules use it as a draft order, for example one granting a certificate of appointment of estate trustee with a will limited to the assets referred to in the will.
civil.74J: Used to apply for a certificate or confirmation of appointment, such as for a foreign estate trustee's nominee without a will, or for a succeeding estate trustee with a will.
civil.74K: The nomination of the applicant by the estate trustee appointed where the deceased was domiciled at death, filed with an application by a foreign estate trustee's nominee.
civil.74L: A bond from an insurer licensed to write surety and fidelity insurance in Ontario, used as the security required by the Estates Act.
civil.74M: A bond from one or more personal sureties, used as the security required by the Estates Act.
civil.74N: The notice the registrar sends, with a copy of the application, to the estate trustee named in a will or codicil deposited with the court when that deposited will prevents confirmation.
civil.74O: The notice the registrar sends to an applicant for a certificate of appointment of estate trustee when the registrar refuses to issue the certificate, or when a notice of objection is filed.
civil.74P: Filed with the registrar by a person with an interest in an estate who wants to be told when a proceeding in the estate starts.
civil.74.43: The estate trustee's affidavit verifying the estate accounts, filed on an application to pass accounts.
civil.74.44: The notice of an application to pass accounts, issued by the court after the estate trustee files the accounts and other material. It states the relief sought, the grounds, and the documentary evidence to be used.
civil.74.45: Served and filed by a person who was served with the accounts documents and wishes to object to the accounts.
civil.74.45.1: A request for further notice in a passing of accounts, served on the applicant and filed with proof of service.
civil.74.46: A notice of no objection to the accounts, one of the documents the Public Guardian and Trustee or the Children's Lawyer, when served in a passing of accounts for a person it represents, serves on the applicant and files.
civil.74.46.1: A notice of non-participation in a passing of accounts, one of the documents the Public Guardian and Trustee or the Children's Lawyer, when served for a person it represents, serves on the applicant and files.
civil.74.47: An affidavit of the applicant or their lawyer, filed to seek judgment on a passing of accounts without a hearing, stating that copies of the accounts went to those who asked, the objection period has expired, and no objection was received or any objection was withdrawn.
civil.74.48: Served and filed by a person who wishes to withdraw a notice of objection to accounts.
civil.74.49: Served and filed by a person, other than the Children's Lawyer or the Public Guardian and Trustee, who was served in a passing of accounts and wishes to seek costs.
civil.74.49.1: Used by the Children's Lawyer or the Public Guardian and Trustee to request costs in a passing of accounts.
civil.74.49.2: Used by an estate trustee seeking costs greater than the amount allowed in Tariff C in a passing of accounts. It states the amount sought, and others return it to object or consent.
civil.74.49.3: Used by a person other than the estate trustee seeking costs greater than the amount allowed in Tariff C in a passing of accounts. It states the amount sought, and others return it to object or consent.
civil.74.49.4: The applicant's reply to notices of objection to accounts, served with a consolidation of the remaining objections when objections are filed and not withdrawn.
civil.74.50: The judgment on a passing of accounts when no one opposes it.
civil.74.51: The judgment on a passing of accounts when it is contested.
civil.74.1A: Used to apply for a small estate certificate, for an estate valued at $150,000 or less. It is filed with other documents the rules list, such as proof of death and a draft certificate.
civil.74.1B: A request filed together with an application for a small estate certificate or an application to amend one.
civil.74.1C: The small estate certificate the registrar may issue. A draft is filed with the application, with a copy of any will and codicils attached.
civil.74.1D: The notice the registrar sends to an applicant for a small estate certificate or amended certificate when the registrar refuses to issue it, or when a notice of objection is filed.
civil.74.1E: Used by the estate trustee named in a small estate certificate to apply for an amended certificate. It is filed with a copy of the issued certificate and a draft amended certificate.
civil.74.1F: The amended small estate certificate. The draft lists both the assets in the original small estate certificate and the additional assets.
civil.75.1: Filed by a person who appears to have a financial interest in an estate, to object before a certificate of appointment of estate trustee is issued. It states the nature of the interest and the objection.
civil.75.3: A notice to objector that an applicant serves on the objector after receiving the notice the rule describes. The applicant also files a copy of it, with proof of service, with the court.
civil.75.4: The notice of appearance an objector serves and files after receiving a notice to objector. If it is not served and filed in time, the application goes ahead as if no objection had been filed.
civil.75.5: Used to start an application for directions. It states the relief sought, the grounds and the evidence, and is served on all persons appearing to have a financial interest in the estate, or as the court directs.
civil.75.6: The notice of a motion for directions, served on all persons appearing to have a financial interest in the estate, or as the court directs.
civil.75.7: A statement of claim that a plaintiff files and serves when an order giving directions says so.
civil.75.8: The form of an order giving directions.
civil.75.10: Served and filed by a defendant, after a statement of claim delivered under an order giving directions, as an alternative to a statement of defence, to submit their rights to the court.
civil.75.11: A notice of settlement personally served on a person who has filed a statement of submission of rights to the court. A lawyer's affidavit can append it to show service and that no rejection of settlement was filed within 10 days, so a consent judgment may be given.
civil.75.12: A rejection of settlement filed with the court by a person who was served with a notice of settlement.
civil.75.13: A notice contesting a claim made against an estate under the Estates Act.
civil.75.14: The form for a claim made against an estate under the Estates Act.
civil.75.1A: Filed with the mediation co-ordinator by the party with carriage of the mediation, to have a mediator assigned when the designated parties have not chosen one in time.
civil.75.1B: The notice a mediator serves on every designated party giving the place, date, time and method of attending the mediation session, and saying attendance is obligatory.
civil.75.1C: A statement each designated party prepares before a mediation session and gives to every other designated party and to the mediator.
civil.75.1D: A certificate the mediator files with the court after cancelling a mediation session that is not practical to conduct because a designated party did not provide the required statement of issues or did not attend within the first 30 minutes.
civil.76A: A notice stating whether the action and related proceedings continue under Rule 76 or as an ordinary action. It is delivered by the plaintiff, or by a party who delivers a jury notice.
civil.76B: The motion form a moving party serves and submits to the court before the motion is brought and heard, in a simplified procedure case.
civil.76C: Served by the plaintiff on every party to the action and filed with proof of service, to set the action down for trial.
civil.76D: A trial management checklist delivered along with a short statement setting out the issues and the party's position on them.
